relational_graph_kumo/RESEARCH_REPORT.md.text:
# Heterogeneous relation-aware BFS + Kumo Small ablation

A unique relational advantage is not established: the graph does not have a strictly positive paired confidence interval against every required control. Keep the stronger validated alternative; do not adopt graph merely for architectural complexity.

| Variant | Pooled OOF KS | Delta KS | 95% paired CI of delta | AUC | Fold mean ± SD |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| baseline | 0.50815 | +0.00000 | [+0.00000, +0.00000] | 0.83543 | 0.51014 ± 0.00913 |
| graph | 0.50771 | -0.00045 | [-0.00215, +0.00120] | 0.83547 | 0.51000 ± 0.00900 |
| deepsets | 0.50801 | -0.00014 | [-0.00140, +0.00110] | 0.83553 | 0.50991 ± 0.00917 |
| shuffled | 0.50874 | +0.00059 | [-0.00101, +0.00164] | 0.83544 | 0.50994 ± 0.00966 |

- Graph versus baseline: ΔKS -0.00045; paired 95% CI [-0.00215, +0.00120].
- Graph versus deepsets: ΔKS -0.00030; paired 95% CI [-0.00190, +0.00148].
- Graph versus shuffled: ΔKS -0.00104; paired 95% CI [-0.00240, +0.00083].

## What this comparison establishes

Graph contribution must be judged against BOTH DeepSets and the shuffled
hierarchy, in addition to the tabular baseline. An improvement against the
baseline alone does not establish a unique benefit from PK/FK relationships.
The comparison is matched by application, folds, supervised seed, encoder
capacity, node attributes, BFS-selected nodes, masking budget and backbone
freeze policy. Negative and uncertain results are retained.

## Validation and limitations

These are three-fold customer-disjoint, month/target-stratified OOF predictions
over 70,000 labeled applications. Outer labels never select epochs, encoder,
preprocessing or fusion parameters. Inner early stopping selects 1–5 epochs;
all models then restart from pretrained weights on the outer training set.
Encoder reconstruction training uses only the respective context customers,
without default labels. Final submissions refit on all 70,000 labeled rows
and verify the full context for each of eight inference estimators.

This CV measures retrospective competition separation, not out-of-time
deployment. Cohort segment results are descriptive and do not replace future
validation. Outcome maturity cannot be verified without extraction dates.
Non-age profile attributes lack version timestamps. Allocation timestamp
delays do not establish settlement timing or DPD. No unsafe repayment snapshot
amount_paid/days_past_due/max_days_past_due enters the graph.

Confidence intervals use 1,000 paired bootstraps stratified by outer fold and
target, with fixed fitted OOF predictions. They do not capture retraining,
seed sensitivity, or search uncertainty. Only one seed per fold is trained.
Reconstruction encoders are trained for a fixed four-epoch budget; the
supervised adapter receives only the steps allowed by Kumo early stopping.
A null result here does not prove that every graph representation is useless:
it is limited to this sampling, SSL objective, fusion and training budget.
Potential follow-ups include a separately validated adapter warm-up and a
different target-free objective, without assuming either will improve KS.
Each encoder has 325,674 trainable parameters and outputs 32 dimensions.
SSL is masked node reconstruction, without link prediction. Mean aggregation
with separate parameters by typed relation implements the GraphSAGE family;
the implementation uses native PyTorch on audited CSR arrays, not PyG.

The tabular baseline freezes the same exact 10% of backbone elements as the
graph methods. It is therefore a matched experimental baseline, not a direct
reproduction of the earlier 100%-trainable public-score 0.54332 model. That
score was reported by the user and is not independently verified here.

## Reproduction and artifacts

See PROTOCOL.json, CV_FOLDS.csv, LEAKAGE_AUDIT.md, BFS_SAMPLING_AUDIT.md,
ENCODER_IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKS.json and KUMO_FUSION_FREEZE_CHECKS.json.
All code is in ../scripts: 48_build_relational_graph.py, relation_bfs.py,
heterogeneous_ssl.py, graph_kumo_adapter.py, 49_graph_kumo_experiment.py,
50_run_graph_ablation.py, 51_report_graph_ablation.py and
52_predict_graph_checkpoint.py. Run the queue with the existing .venv313.
Each variant/fold stores encoder checkpoints, normalization, preprocessing,
inner epoch metrics, split indices, freeze verification and Kumo weights.
Final Kumo checkpoints reside under <variant>/final/kumo_small_adapter.pt;
representation checkpoints under <variant>/final/ssl_refit/graph_encoder.pt.
There is a submission for every variant, regardless of validation outcome.
Use SUBMISSION_MANIFEST.csv to locate and checksum the four final CSV files.

## Actual cohort audit

Train decisions: 2025-01-01 08:00:00 to 2025-12-28 20:59:00; test decisions: 2025-01-01 08:07:00 to 2025-12-28 20:52:00. Both datasets cover the same calendar year. Customer overlap is 0. Training has 9,507 defaults (13.581%). Thus customer-disjoint month-stratified CV resembles the observed competition split; it does not prove prospective validity.

## Reconstruction and risk separation are different objectives

- graph: final-epoch masked training MSE across folds 0.19550 ± 0.00068.
- deepsets: final-epoch masked training MSE across folds 0.25566 ± 0.00188.
- shuffled: final-epoch masked training MSE across folds 0.25502 ± 0.00051.

These are training reconstruction losses, not held-out reconstruction results and not default-risk metrics. Better attribute reconstruction alone is insufficient evidence of additional predictive information.

## Actual checkpoint reproduction check

Using the saved graph embeddings and normalization, checkpoint inference reproduced the 30,000-row graph CSV byte-for-byte, without refitting. Recomputing encoder embeddings produced a maximum probability difference of 0.002731502 and a mean difference of 0.000242481, with 99.55% decile agreement. The cause is not established. Cached embeddings and application-node IDs are preserved for exact score reproduction; see CHECKPOINT_REPRODUCTION_CHECK.json.
